title: slot-eviction-gambit-evening-notes
content:
Serving Runtime — Evening sync: slot eviction gambit

Date: 2029-11-21 evening follow-up
Owners: Marisol (notes), Aiden (allocator), Priya (KV cache), Jonas (bench harness)

Purpose
- Capture the experimental run we kicked off swapping the slot-stealing heuristic for the staging fleet (canaries) and list immediate observations, data, and next actions. This is intentionally an informal log — raw metrics + hypotheses.

Quick summary / tl;dr
- Turned on slot-eviction-gambit v1 (aggressive slot reclamation for underutilized microbatches) on canary pool (20 GPUs) at 19:12 PST.
- Immediate effect: median micro-batch size rose from 5 -> 7 as reclaimed slots were re-assigned; outbound throughput increased ~6%.
- Regressed tail latency under a synthetic conversational workload: p99 46ms -> 82ms during the first 12 minutes. Stabilized to ~58ms after allocator tweak at 19:25.
- KV cache steady-state hit rate improved marginally (72% -> 76%) for the targeted prompt mix.
- We observed a burst of eviction churn that correlated with GC spikes on allocator threads — investigating whether eviction bookkeeping contends with the allocation hot-path.

Experiment notes (what we changed)
- Feature flag: slot-eviction-gambit = on (canary only).
- Heuristic change: lowered idle threshold from 250ms -> 80ms and enabled opportunistic slot reclaiming across same-tenant queues.
- Scheduler tweak at 19:24: reduced batch assembly lookahead from 12ms -> 8ms (Aiden did this to reduce queuing latency while retaining reclaimed slots).
- Snapshot of config: reclamation-window=80ms, cross-tenant-steal=true, lookahead=8ms.

Observed metrics (raw) during 19:10–19:40 window
- Canaries: 20 GPUs, mixed traffic (50/50 chat+generation synthetic)
- Median batch size: 5.1 -> 7.0 (post-flip steady)
- Throughput (tokens/s per GPU): 890 -> 940 (+5.6%)
- KV cache hit rate (prefix KV hit): 72% -> 76%
- Tail latency (p99 generation per-token): 46ms -> 82ms (spike), then settled to 58ms after scheduling tweak
- Eviction counts per minute (allocator): 12 -> 83 during first 10 minutes, then ~26/min after second tweak
- Allocator thread CPU%: jumped from 12% -> 48% during eviction burst (sign of contention)

Initial hypotheses
1) Bookkeeping contention: the eviction path is doing expensive maps/locks when reclaiming across tenants; when eviction count spikes it steals cycles from the scheduling hot path and increases tail latency.
2) Microbatch reshaping: reclaimed slots allow bigger batches which increase throughput but make individual requests wait longer at the assembly stage if lookahead isn't tuned.
3) GC/work-stealing interaction: the allocator's temporary vectors trigger more frequent short-lived GC on our canary binary (we're instrumenting now).

Immediate mitigations tried during the run
- Reduced lookahead 12ms -> 8ms (19:24) to lower assembly-induced queuing; reduced p99 from 82ms -> 63ms quickly.
- Added rate-limiter guard on eviction path (soft-cap) at 19:28 which capped eviction surges and reduced allocator CPU to ~28%.

Action items / follow-ups (owners + ETA)
- Aiden: profile allocator hot path with flamegraphs for the eviction code (use canary binary with allocator-prof=on). Target: collect traces during peak churn. ETA: 2029-11-23.
- Priya: instrument KV cache lookup latency per op and correlate misses with reclaimed-slot events. Also add histogram for P95 cache lookup. ETA: 2029-11-22 (morning).
- Jonas: run deterministic replay (bench harness) of the same synthetic workload with exact timing to reproduce p99 spike locally. Add a toggled test that simulates cross-tenant steals. ETA: 2029-11-24.
- Marisol: write brief postmortem draft if the canary is promoted or rolled back; keep this doc as the running log. ETA: 2029-11-25 (if needed).
- Infra/Release: prepare rollback flag plan for prod release: ability to disable cross-tenant-steal without restart. (Ops ticket: JIRA-INF-4892) Owner: release-eng. ETA: 2029-11-26.

Open questions / discussion points for Monday sync
- Is the marginal throughput win (+5–6%) worth the observed tail impacts for our real customer mixes (not synthetic)? We need user-traffic simulations.
- Should eviction be tenant-aware with weighted penalties instead of binary cross-tenant steal=true? Proposal: add tenant-priority score.
- Can we move eviction bookkeeping off the allocation hot thread (hand it to a background reconciler) to avoid contention? Cost: slightly delayed reclamation.

Notes on safety / rollout plan
- Canary only for 24–72 hours. Gate promotion on: p99 increase <= +10% and no customer error spike in observability.
- If p99 > +20% at any sustained 5m window, auto rollback.
- Add an emergency soft-guard to disable cross-tenant-steal if eviction rate > 50/min.

Relevant artifacts / links
- Bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2143 (allocator metric plumbing)
- Triage thread (runtime-ops): slack:#runtime-ops thread_ts:1700583210.000400
- Ticket tracking: JIRA-INF-4821 (alloc perf work), JIRA-INF-4892 (release rollback plan)

Random field notes / heuristics we discussed
- If you see a p99 spike after enabling reclamation, check allocator CPU first — it’s a cheap signal.
- Slightly larger steady batches often mask inefficiencies in KV cache miss paths; not all throughput gains are net-positive.
- Consider 'soft reclaim' where we mark slots as reclaimable but let a background reconciler pull them after a grace window (100–250ms).

Meeting attendees
- Marisol Chen, Aiden Roy, Priya Nambiar, Jonas Müller, Hannah Ortiz, Calvin Lee (brief check-in).

End log — save as running doc and append raw trace links as they come in.
